issue.title: Gmail archive -c digest and frozen closes bind task line numbers, so unrelated vault edits void confirmation
issue.description:
## Root cause

`plan_digest` (src/native/gmail/sync/archive_preview.rs) hashes a `DigestTask {path, line,
block_id, status}` for every linking task (DIGEST_VERSION = 1). The task's 1-based LINE
number is therefore part of the confirmation digest. Any vault edit that shifts lines
above a linking task, even in an unrelated part of the file, voids a pending
`bob gmail sync -c <digest>`, although nothing semantic changed. This fails closed (no
data risk). But the `-d` → review → `-c` workflow, including the hourly cron's own
"confirm with: bob gmail sync -c …" hint, is brittle for someone who edits task files all
day.

Same root cause, second surface (verify): `ArchiveTaskLocator`
(src/native/gmail/sync/archive_state.rs) also carries `line`. `fresh_matches_close`
(archive_apply.rs) compares fresh locators to the frozen close's `tasks`, so a journaled
close generation whose apply is retried after a line shift is held rather than archived.

## Likely remedy

Bind `block_id` when the linking task has one, and fall back to the line number (or a
hash of the normalized task text) only when it has none. Apply this to both the digest
and the frozen-close locator comparison, and bump DIGEST_VERSION. Old journaled closes
must still fold: keep `line` in stored events, but stop comparing it when a block id
is present.

## Acceptance

- In a fixture where every linking task has a block id, inserting lines above a linking
  task changes neither the `-d` digest nor the `-c` outcome.
- A task without a block id keeps today's fail-closed behavior.
- Existing `gmail.archive_closed` journal events still fold.

task_type_fields.impact: Fail-closed (no data risk), but any edit above a linked task voids a pending 'bob gmail sync -c <digest>' (backlog and burst confirmations), forcing a re-preview and re-approval; kx.5 needed a second gate.
task_type_fields.location: src/native/gmail/sync/archive_preview.rs DigestTask/plan_digest; src/native/gmail/sync/archive_state.rs ArchiveTaskLocator; archive_apply.rs fresh_matches_close
task_type_fields.repro:
Observed live on the Mac writer during bob-cli-kx.5 (2026-11-14, pinned build 11abff0b):

1. 09:5x EST: `bob gmail sync -d -f json` (read-only) returned 9 backlog rows and digest
   76224b9f422ef64cf0d1dd2e132442b15c2b0afd33d01a7474d9537988a5e4a7. Bryan approved that
   exact set in a gate.
2. Within the next 2 minutes Bryan edited sase.md (vault commits 60033e4b2 09:52:53 and
   bb7b08667 09:54:00) and inserted 3 lines above task ^try-fable-5-2. That moved the task
   from sase.md:592 to :595. The task links thread 1a1c57d9dc91041d (kept:consent_removed).
3. 09:54 EST: `bob gmail sync -c 76224b9f… -f json` exited 1. All 9 rows came back
   `paused: confirm_mismatch`, and nothing was archived. Every other bound field was
   byte-identical. A fresh preview produced a new digest (9f5df929…), and a second gate was
   needed. Its wrapper compared the approved set with line numbers ignored before
   confirming.

Local repro: in a fixture vault with one closed backlog row, run `sync -d -f json` and note
`archive_digest`. Insert a blank line above the linking task (no other change). Then
`sync -c <digest>` exits 1 with `confirm_mismatch`.

The indirect dependency is newly projected close.generation -> task_values(line), despite DIGEST_VERSION 2. Repair remains on active epic bob-cli-lk.
